I am so very grateful to have had parents willing to support me through college; however, my parents and I got into a huge fight over this past New Years Eve. My parents are strict conservatives and bible beating folk. My irresponsible, 22-year-old self got wasted at our neighbors' house and accidentally passed out on their couch (however, no one saw - no harm done right?! jk.... :/ ). Needless to say, I managed to anger them enough that they are "no longer are willing to support me," and want me to pay for everything on my own "alcoholic-self." They are however, willing to reimburse me for A's. The only problem is, how the goddamned fuck am I supposed to pull roughly $40,000 out of my mother fucking ass? I have mildly shitty credit (about a 600 I think.. or less. who the fuck knows), and I'm not sure if they would be willing to co-sign on a loan since I am "on my own." My parents make wayyy too much money for me to get any sort of need-based scholarship, and I haven't reached the age where I don't have to put them on my FASFA. I know I sound like a spoiled thundercunt, and I can assure you I am. I just need a love kick in the ass towards the right direction. I need to know, is there any possibility I can even get that much money in loans? What do I say to my bank? I was getting monthly allowances, but now that that has been cut off, I have an almost maxed out $1000 limit on my card right now and almost nothing in my other account. I have no job either - at least not yet anyway. I was even considering joining the military to get free college later, but not sure how that would go over whilst I'm trying to mend my relationship with my family (or if I would even make it). Also that would set me back from graduating several years back, and I'm so close right now. I am fearful of a mega-assfucking. I need any advice I can get. I will be forever grateful. Peace be with you.
(Repost from v/NoStupidQuestions, thought it fit better here.) How do I go about paying for college with shitty credit, possibly no cosigner, and no eligibility for scholarships/grants?

Well first off, I would go to your financial aid office or whatever equivalent you have there. They have all your records and will be much more helpful with letting you know exactly what options you have available. Not sure what kind of loans you'll be able to get, especially if your parents are genuinely serious about completely cutting you off. If you can't get loans out, there might be some online scholarships that you can write some essays and such for, but nowhere near 40K's worth. Really, you're pretty limited and you may just have to drop out until you either mend your issue with your parents or get a job and save up the rest of the money on your own. Definitely check the financial aid office first though before anything else.

I'm assuming you live in the US. Your financial aid office can help you get a loan. Government guaranteed loans are available regardless of your credit rating, without a co-signer as long as your college is accredited and your grades are C or higher. You'll be fine.
